brief.goal: Explain solar panels, daily energy patterns, and battery storage using the provided synthetic example
keyPoints: Solar panels convert sunlight into electricity
Daily energy pattern: Morning (10 Wh), Noon (20 Wh), Evening (5 Wh)
Batteries store electricity for use after sunset
constraints: Use only the provided synthetic example from solar-facts.csv
openQuestions: What specific teaching objectives should be emphasized?
Are there any particular misconceptions about solar energy we should address?

flow.title: Solar Energy Basics
flow.summary: An introduction to solar energy, explaining how panels convert sunlight into electricity, the daily energy pattern throughout the day, and how batteries store energy for use after sunset.

beats.title: How Panels Work
beats.audienceText: Solar panels convert sunlight directly into electricity.
beats.speakerNotes: Explain that solar panels contain photovoltaic cells that absorb photons from sunlight and convert them into electrical energy.
beats.visualDirection: Show the flow diagram illustrating how Sun energy moves through Panels to generate electricity stored in Battery.

beats.title: Daily Energy Pattern
beats.audienceText: Energy production peaks at noon, with lower output in the morning and evening.
beats.speakerNotes: Point to the bar chart showing Morning (10 Wh), Noon (20 Wh), and Evening (5 Wh) energy levels. Emphasize that this is a synthetic teaching example.
beats.visualDirection: Display the bar chart of daily energy production to illustrate the pattern throughout the day.

beats.title: Storage After Sunset
beats.audienceText: Batteries store excess electricity for use when the sun is not shining.
beats.speakerNotes: Refer back to the flow diagram, highlighting how energy stored in the Battery can be used after sunset. Explain that this storage capability is crucial for consistent power supply.
beats.visualDirection: Use the flow diagram again to show how Panels generate energy that gets stored in Battery for later use.

openQuestions: What specific teaching objectives should be emphasized?
Are there any particular misconceptions about solar energy we should address?

flow.title: Solar Energy Basics
flow.summary: An introduction to solar energy, explaining how panels convert sunlight into electricity, the daily energy pattern throughout the day, and how batteries store energy for use after sunset.

beats.title: How Panels Work
beats.audienceText: Solar panels convert sunlight directly into electricity.
beats.speakerNotes: Explain that solar panels contain photovoltaic cells that absorb photons from sunlight and convert them into electrical energy.
beats.visualDirection: Show the flow diagram illustrating how Sun energy moves through Panels to generate electricity stored in Battery.

beats.title: Daily Energy Pattern
beats.audienceText: Energy production peaks at noon, with lower output in the morning and evening.
beats.speakerNotes: Point to the bar chart showing Morning (10 Wh), Noon (20 Wh), and Evening (5 Wh) energy levels. Emphasize that this is a synthetic teaching example.
beats.visualDirection: Display the bar chart of daily energy production to illustrate the pattern throughout the day.

beats.title: Storage After Sunset
beats.audienceText: Batteries store excess electricity for use when the sun is not shining.
beats.speakerNotes: Refer back to the flow diagram, highlighting how energy stored in the Battery can be used after sunset. Explain that this storage capability is crucial for consistent power supply.
beats.visualDirection: Use the flow diagram again to show how Panels generate energy that gets stored in Battery for later use.

Are there any particular misconceptions about solar energy we should address?
